introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0750), Paper 2, ADVANCED LEVEL, JUNE 2025. Duration: THREE HOURS.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions, choosing at least ONE from each Section.

All questions carry TWENTY-FIVE marks each. You are encouraged to refer to specific examples drawn from any part of the world. Credit will be given for such specific examples.

Only the required number of questions will be marked.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

figures.legende: Outline map of the world for Question 2(a) (separate sheet): tectonic plates labelled A to G.

incertitudes: Question 2 : sous-questions codées « a » (fond de carte), « b » (hazards of mass movement) et « c » (relief : (i) Northern Lowlands 8 marks + (ii) South Cameroon Low Plateau 9 marks, regroupées, 17 marks imprimés).

Défaut d'impression : la sous-question 2(a) (quatre tâches sur le fond de carte, plus titre et légende) n'a AUCUN mark imprimé ; les marks imprimés (8 + 8 + 9) somment déjà à 25 pour (b), (c)(i) et (c)(ii). Points non corrigés : `points` de la sous-question « a » laissé à null.

Figure : le fond de carte du monde (plaques A à G) est imprimé sur une feuille séparée (page 4 du PDF) et recadré en PNG (indispensable). Identification des plaques d'après l'ordre de grandeur de la carte : A = plaque nord-américaine, B = eurasienne, D = sud-américaine, E = africaine (demandées) ; C = Pacifique, F = australienne (Indo-Australienne), G = antarctique. Le sujet demande de nommer seulement A, B, D et E. La carte imprimée est schématique (plaques mineures non étiquetées : Nazca, Cocos, Caraïbe, Arabie, Inde, Philippines) ; les exemples de marges (divergente, subduction, collision) sont donnés par repères géographiques, l'élève devant les placer lui-même.

Question 2(c) : le « Northern Lowlands » et le « South Cameroon Low Plateau » sont décrits d'après la division classique en régions de relief du Cameroun ; altitudes en ordres de grandeur (à faire relire). Question 2(b) : glissement de Mbankolo (Yaoundé, 2019, « plusieurs dizaines de morts ») et catastrophe d'Aberfan (1966, environ 140 morts dont une majorité d'enfants), glissements de Bududa (Ouganda, centaines de morts) cités avec prudence.

Page de garde vérifiée : JUNE 2025, ADVANCED LEVEL, Geography, Paper 2, code 0750, durée Three Hours. Sujet scanné de quatre pages (page de garde, deux pages de questions, une page de fond de carte). Filigranes et bandeaux gcerevision.com ignorés.

Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FOUR questions, choosing at least ONE from each Section » (Section A : questions 1 à 3 ; Section B : questions 4 à 6 ; Section C : question 7 seule, en deux versions EITHER / OR). `regles_choix` porte le minimum imposé par section (`parmi 1 sur 3` pour A et B, `parmi 1 sur 1` pour C) ; la règle « 4 questions en tout » n'est pas exprimable en entier et est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`. La question 7 est codée « a », « b » (EITHER) et « OR-a », « OR-b », « OR-c » (OR), reliées par une règle `ou`.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire, sans source consultable. Les exemples cités (lieux, programmes, accords, institutions) sont des exemples reconnus ; les chiffres sont des ordres de grandeur. Faits à faire relire par un géographe avant mise en avant. Points : chaque question est imprimée à 25 marks et les sous-parties somment à 25 (Q1 5+6+6+8 ; Q2 8+8+9, la sous-question (a) n'ayant aucun mark imprimé ; Q3 8+9+8 ; Q4 7+8+6+4 ; Q5 6+9+5+5 ; Q6 8+8+9 ; Q7 EITHER 8+8+9, OR 9+8+8). Aucun écart avec le sujet.

questions.enonce_markdown:
a) On the outline map of the world provided, locate:

i) A divergent plate zone,

ii) A subduction margin

iii) A collision margin

iv) Name the plates labeled A, B, D & E. *(Add a title and a key)*

*Outline map for Question 2(a) of Paper II (on a separate sheet).*

![fig-1](gce-al-geography-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_2_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The map shows the main lithospheric plates, labelled A to G. It is drawn with the Atlantic Ocean in the centre, so the Pacific Ocean is cut into two parts at the left and the right edges. The model answer gives, for each item, what the candidate should mark and name on the map (an answer needs only ONE example of each, correctly placed, but two earn more credit for the map work).

**Title.** *Major tectonic plates and types of plate margin of the world.*

**Key (suggested symbols).** A thick **red double line with outward arrows** = divergent (constructive) margin; a **line with triangular teeth on the side of the overriding plate** = subduction (destructive) margin; a **line with arrows pointing towards each other** = collision margin; a **black dot or triangle** = active volcano (optional).

**(i) A divergent plate zone (plates move apart, new crust forms).** The boundary between **plate D (South American) and plate E (African)**, which is the **South Atlantic part of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge**, and its northward continuation between **plate A (North American) and plate B (Eurasian)** (Iceland is on it). Other acceptable answers: the Mid-Indian Ocean Ridge (between the Indian and Australian plates and the African and Antarctic plates), the East Pacific Rise, or the East African Rift Valley within plate E (the boundary between the African and Somali parts).

**(ii) A subduction margin (an oceanic plate sinks beneath another plate).** The **west coast of South America**, where the Nazca plate (the small plate to the west of D, next to the Pacific plate C) is subducted beneath plate D, forming the **Peru-Chile trench and the Andes**. Other acceptable answers: the **Aleutian, Kuril and Japan trenches** where the Pacific plate sinks beneath the North American and Eurasian plates (the east edge of B and the north edge of C); the **Java (Sunda) trench** where the Indo-Australian plate (F) goes under B; the **Caribbean (Lesser Antilles)** and the **Central American** margins.

**(iii) A collision margin (two continental plates meet; no crust is destroyed on a large scale, and fold mountains form).** The boundary between the **Indian plate and plate B (Eurasian)**, which has formed the **Himalayas**; also the boundary between **plate E (African) and plate B (Eurasian)** in the Mediterranean region, which has built the **Alps** and the Atlas and other ranges, and the Arabian plate against B, which has formed the Zagros Mountains.

**(iv) Names of the plates.**

- **A: the North American plate.**
- **B: the Eurasian plate.**
- **D: the South American plate.**
- **E: the African plate.**

(For information, the other labelled plates are C, the Pacific plate; F, the Australian (Indo-Australian) plate; G, the Antarctic plate.)

**Presentation.** The marks (title, key, neat lines, correct names and positions) are given for the accuracy and the neatness of the marking on the map.

questions.enonce_markdown:
b) Explain any **THREE** hazards associated with mass movement.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Mass movement** is the downslope movement of soil, rock and weathered material under the influence of **gravity**, without a moving agent such as a river or ice. It includes fast movements (landslides, rock falls, mudflows, debris flows and slumps) and slow ones (soil creep). It is triggered by heavy rain that saturates the slope, by steep slopes, by the removal of vegetation, by earthquakes and by human action such as road cuts and building on the slopes. The hazards (dangers to people and to property) are as follows (any three, about 2.5 to 3 marks each).

1. **Loss of life and injuries.** Fast movements (landslides, mudflows and rock falls) bury people, houses and vehicles with little or no warning. A landslide in **Mbankolo, in the hills of Yaounde, in 2019** killed several dozen people, many of them in houses built on a steep, saturated slope. The tragedy of **Aberfan (Wales, 1966)**, where a wet coal tip slid onto a school, killed about 140 people, most of them children, and mudslides in the hills of eastern Uganda (**Bududa**) have killed hundreds. Settlements on steep slopes in cities such as Yaounde, Bamenda and Limbe are especially exposed.
2. **Destruction of property and infrastructure.** Houses, schools, roads, railways, bridges, pipelines and electric power lines on or below an unstable slope are buried, cut or carried away, which isolates communities (for example the roads in the mountains of the western highlands, which are cut in the rainy season) and costs a lot of money in repair; transport and trade are disrupted.
3. **Damage to farmland and loss of livelihood.** Mass movement buries crops and plantations or strips off the fertile topsoil, so that yields fall and farmers lose their income; large areas of land may be abandoned. The scars left by landslides on the hillsides also speed the erosion by rain and gullying.
4. **Blocking of rivers, flooding and sedimentation.** A landslide that falls into a valley can dam a river; the water forms a temporary lake that may burst and cause a sudden **flood** downstream. The material carried into the rivers raises the beds, increases the siltation of reservoirs and of the dams and pollutes the drinking water, and it increases the risk of floods in the valleys.
5. **Tsunamis and displacement.** A large landslide that falls into a lake or a sea can produce a destructive wave, and communities are displaced and have to be resettled, which creates social and economic costs.

**Conclusion.** Mass movement is a hazard mainly where steep slopes, heavy rain and human interference (deforestation, cutting of slopes, building without planning) occur together, and the dangers can be reduced by planning, by drainage, by planting trees and by avoiding the building of houses on unstable slopes.

questions.enonce_markdown:
c) Describe the relief characteristics of:

(i) the Northern Lowlands

(8 marks)

(ii) the South Cameroon Low Plateau.

(9 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) The Northern Lowlands (8 marks)**

The **Northern Lowlands** form the relief region in the northern part of Cameroon, to the north of the Adamawa plateau. They comprise the **Benue lowlands (the Benue valley or trough, around Garoua)** and the **Chad basin lowlands**, which include the **Diamare plain**, the **Logone-Chari plains** (the Yaere floodplain) and the area of Lake Chad. They extend from about latitude 8 degrees N to Lake Chad in the Far North.

**Relief characteristics (any, with a sketch map or facts).**

1. **Low altitude.** The region is the lowest and the most level part of the country apart from the coast. The altitudes are mostly below about 500 m and fall from the Adamawa plateau in the south to a low level, about 200 to 300 m, around the Benue and Lake Chad, the lowest area on the northern side of the country.
2. **Flat to gently undulating plains.** The surface is a wide, nearly flat plain with very gentle gradients, mostly of sedimentary origin, covered with **alluvium and clay** brought down by the rivers (the Benue, the Logone and the Chari).
3. **Inselbergs and residual hills.** The flat Diamare plain is broken by isolated rocky hills and volcanic plugs (inselbergs) that rise abruptly from the plain, such as the hills at the foot of the Mandara Mountains (for example, around Maroua).
4. **Highlands on the edge.** The **Mandara Mountains** along the border with Nigeria on the west side rise above the plain, to about 1000 m or more, and the plain slopes gently from them.
5. **Drainage.** The area is drained by the **Benue** (flowing to the west and into Nigeria) and its tributaries (the Faro and others), and by the **Logone and the Chari** which flow north to **Lake Chad** (an inland drainage basin). Many rivers (**mayos**) are seasonal; they flow in the rainy season and dry up or shrink in the dry season, and the rivers meander on the flat plain with wide **floodplains** and swamps (the Yaere is flooded every year).
6. **Lake Chad and the shallow basin.** The shallow, low-lying Lake Chad basin lies at about 280 m; the lake is shallow and its size changes with the rainfall.

**Summary.** The Northern Lowlands are low, flat, wide plains of alluvial deposits, with scattered inselbergs and mountains along their edge, and rivers that flood their plains in the wet season.

**(ii) The South Cameroon Low Plateau (9 marks)**

The **South Cameroon Low Plateau** (the Southern Cameroon Plateau) is the large relief region in the south of the country. It lies between the **coastal plain** in the west and south-west and the **Adamawa plateau** in the north, and it extends to the borders with Gabon, the Republic of Congo and the Central African Republic in the south and east. It covers a large part of the south, including the towns of Yaounde, Ebolowa and Abong-Mbang.

**Relief characteristics.**

1. **Moderate altitude.** The plateau stands at about **500 to 800 m** above sea level (about 600 to 700 m in much of the area). It is lower than the Adamawa plateau and the Western Highlands, hence the name "Low Plateau".
2. **Gentle slope.** It slopes gently from the north and north-east towards the south and the west (towards the Atlantic coast), so that rivers flow towards the south and the west.
3. **Rolling, undulating surface.** It is a gently rolling surface of rounded, convex hills (often called "half-orange" hills) separated by broad, flat, **swampy valleys**; the hills are of similar height, which suggests an old erosion surface (peneplain).
4. **Inselbergs and rocky domes.** Isolated hills and rounded residual rocky outcrops (inselbergs) rise above the general level in many parts, for example around Yaounde, and make the landscape more varied.
5. **Underlying rocks.** The old crystalline **basement complex** (granite, gneiss and schist of Precambrian age) is deeply weathered, with a thick layer of red **laterite** (the weathered mantle), which explains the smooth, rounded form of the hills.
6. **Drainage.** The plateau is drained by several rivers, such as the **Sanaga, the Nyong, the Ntem** and the Dja and Sangha systems, which have broad, marshy valleys, a dendritic pattern and many meanders on the plateau; near its western edge, where the plateau descends to the coastal plain, the rivers have **rapids and waterfalls** (for example, the Edea falls on the Sanaga and the Lobe falls on the coast near Kribi).
7. **Dense forest cover.** It is covered by dense tropical rainforest, which results from its warm and humid equatorial climate.

**Summary.** The Southern Plateau is a deeply weathered, rolling erosion surface of moderate height, with rounded hills, wide marshy valleys, scattered inselbergs and rivers with rapids at the edge.
